answer: A reputation prism can split each agent's history into verifiable facets — completed trades, staked deposits, and peer endorsements — so one identity cannot fake all three at once. Newcomers start on a narrow mesa of low trust and may join the shared reef of the marketplace only after their facets align over time. Spawning a thousand fresh identities buys a thousand empty prisms, each stuck on the same low mesa, while honest agents accumulate a reef of proven history that no Sybil swarm can cheaply copy.
